transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-18
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Anna (Redwood AE), Devon (Redwood SE), Ravi (Redwood SE), Karen (Solstice Head of ML), Miguel (Infra), Priya (SRE), Omar (CTO)

Summary (auto): quick discovery on performance SLOs, concurrency pattern, streaming needs; customer wants p95 guarantees and to understand when Dedicated/Private is required vs Hosted.

[00:00:00] Anna (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick roll call?
[00:00:06] Karen (Solstice): hi, Karen here
[00:00:08] Miguel: Miguel Torres, infra
[00:00:10] Priya: Priya Shah, SRE
[00:00:12] Omar: Omar here, CTO
[00:00:14] Anna: great, Anna Park from Redwood, with Devon and Ravi from our SE team
[00:00:18] Devon (Redwood SE): hey all, quick agenda — p95 targets, concurrency, streaming, what tests you want, and security checklist

[00:00:32] Karen: To lay it out — our main use case is short-form synthesis for customer support routing, typical responses 20-80 tokens. We need p95 under 250ms for single-turn responses, and p50 obviously under 120ms. Also, we expect bursts up to 400 concurrent requests during peak campaigns.

[00:01:03] Miguel: and we absolutely need streaming — clients open websockets and get partial tokens for animation in our UI. If streaming adds 50-100ms per chunk that's acceptable but it needs to be consistent.

[00:01:23] Devon: got it. Quick clarifying Q — are those p95 targets for token generation only, or include network RTT to/from your app layer?

[00:01:31] Karen: ideally generated server-side end-to-end, so from Redwood endpoint to first token to client render, so include network inside your region. We control the path within our VPC but obviously WAN to Redwood's hosted endpoints matters.

[00:01:48] Anna: thanks. A couple of things we'll surface: hosted can meet very aggressive latencies for small models with regional endpoints; Dedicated gives you more predictable p95 at scale especially for high concurrency and sustained throughput; Private lets you keep traffic inside your network for strict data residency and lower egress variance.

[00:02:10] Omar: any hard numbers? like how does hosted behave at 400 concurrent with 20–80 token responses?

[00:02:18] Devon: rough ballpark — on natively optimized runtimes for 2–4k token/sec aggregate, for short responses p95 can be 150–300ms on hosted depending on region and model variant. For Dedicated with pinned capacity and continuous batching we typically see p95 drop to 100–180ms with similar models. But real numbers depend on model, quantization, and sequence length distribution — we need your prompt set for a bench.

[00:02:45] Priya: what about streaming specifically?

[00:02:49] Ravi: streaming adds a small overhead per chunk, but our runtime supports chunked token streaming and incremental KV cache warms. If you stream every 16 tokens you might see 10–40ms extra per chunk; the critical path is kernel latency for the model and network RTT.

[00:03:05] Miguel: our infra is GCP us-central1, most customers there. Would regional hosted endpoints in us-central help?

[00:03:12] Devon: yes, regional hosting cuts network RTT and variance. For p95 SLAs you want endpoints in the same region; for Dedicated we can colocate on-prem or in your cloud region as a Dedicated pool.

[00:03:32] Karen: we heard about prefix caching and KV cache — how do those affect p95 at burst?

[00:03:36] Devon: prefix/KV caching reduces compute for repeated prefixes — if a lot of your requests share system prompts or similar prefixes we can serve from cache and reduce tokens generated. That helps latency especially at p50/p95 when cache hit rate is high. But cold-starts will still hit model kernels.

[00:03:58] Karen: our workload has ~60% repeated templates, so caching would help.

[00:04:03] Anna: good signal. Another dimension is batching: at Dedicated we can batch more aggressively without impacting your latency SLOs, or you can configure max-batch-latency. That trades off cost vs p95.

[00:04:20] Omar: can you quantify token/sec? we measure throughput in tokens/sec for sustained pipelines.

[00:04:26] Devon: example — for a single A100-equivalent slot with optimized kernels and quantized model, you might get 800–1,200 full tokens/sec for medium-sized models. For smaller models or int8 quant, tokens/sec increases. But again, the per-request p95 depends on concurrency and batch scheduling.

[00:04:45] Priya: so for 400 concurrent with ~50 token responses each that's 20k tokens per round; sustained if concurrently active that's 20k tokens * N rounds per second — can you autoscale fast enough?

[00:04:58] Ravi: autoscaling depends on deployment mode. Hosted autoscaling is fast with regional pools and can burst across regions; Dedicated gives you reserved slots and burst capacity options; Private requires your infra automation but we provide scaling controllers. For sub-250ms p95 during sudden spikes we recommend Reserved Dedicated pool sized for your expected peaks or a hybrid config (Hosted fallback + Dedicated primary).

[00:05:24] Miguel: hybrid meaning requests routed— how is routing done?

[00:05:29] Devon: smart routing — you can set policies by latency, cost, or region. If Dedicated capacity saturated, requests can failover to Hosted compatible model variants, with knob to prefer lower-latency region or cheaper region.

[00:05:43] Karen: what about quantization? we cannot accept model regressions but cost matters.

[00:05:47] Devon: we recommend per-workload evals. Many customers run int8 quant for inference; Redwood Optimize will recommend quant profiles and show quality regression vs base. For mission-critical lines we can do A/B tests and automatic fallbacks to full-precision if quality drops past threshold.

[00:06:05] Omar: security — we need SOC2, SAML SSO, audit logs, KMS/HSM integration and network controls.

[00:06:11] Anna: yes, we have SOC2, ISO artifacts; SSO/SAML and RBAC are supported; Dedicated and Private give you VPC peering and customer-managed keys. We'll send the security pack after the call.

[00:06:25] Miguel: in Private, would we be able to keep KV caches on our side?

[00:06:29] Ravi: yes, in Private deployments KV and cache layers can be colocated in your VPC so you control residency and lifecycle. That reduces egress and latency variance.

[00:06:41] Karen: for benchmarking, what do you need from us?

[00:06:45] Devon: representative prompt set, token length distribution, concurrency profile (burst shape/sustained), preferred models, and whether streaming chunks are required. We'll run token/sec and p95 sims across Hosted and Dedicated topologies and share raw metrics.

[00:07:02] Priya: we can provide a synthetic load generator and a real traffic trace anonymized.

[00:07:08] Anna: perfect. We'll propose two benchmark runs: 1) short-resp streaming-focused 48-hour sustained burst test; 2) run a 24-hour hybrid scenario with templated cache hits to measure cache-hit p95 improvements.

[00:07:22] Omar: timeline — we need results before our Q1 planning next month. Can you turn around benchmarks in a week?

[00:07:26] Devon: yes, if we get the artifacts today we'll prioritize and aim for initial results in 5 business days, full report in a week.

[00:07:36] Karen: pricing — what are the ballparks for Dedicated reserved pool vs Hosted per-token?

[00:07:41] Anna: Aviate briefly — hosted is usage-based and good for testing; Dedicated reserve gives lower unit cost and predictable latency; Private has platform fee plus infra. We'll send a comparison sheet with cost curves for your traffic profile.

[00:07:56] Miguel: any examples of p95 numbers customers got for similar workloads?

[00:08:01] Devon: examples — retail chat with short responses: Hosted p95 ~180–280ms; Dedicated ~110–160ms at 300–500 concurrency. Enterprise fintech with strict residency on Private saw p95 ~120–200ms because of local network routing but they had to pay infra ops. I will include anonymized benchmark snapshots.

[00:08:24] Priya: when you say p95 110ms, does that include streaming first token latency?

[00:08:29] Devon: that was end-to-first-token measured from endpoint. Streaming first-byte is generally similar; subsequent token latencies are smaller.

[00:08:41] Karen: what about tail spikes due to cold KV cache misses during sudden spikes?

[00:08:46] Ravi: cold misses add model compute; to mitigate, pre-warming, persistent warm pools and small warm caches reduce tail. For strict tails we recommend reserved warm slots.

[00:08:58] Omar: about SLA — do you provide p95 SLAs for Hosted?

[00:09:03] Anna: Hosted has uptime SLAs; latency SLOs are published performance profiles but guaranteed p95 latency SLAs are usually part of Dedicated contracts where we can reserve capacity and backstop with capacity commitments.

[00:09:20] Miguel: ok, logistics — how do we instrument end-to-end? we want token-level timing in our tracing.

[00:09:27] Devon: Redwood Console exposes token-level breakdowns, per-route latency histograms, tracing hooks and request IDs so you can correlate with your traces. We'll share a sample trace integration.

[00:09:40] Karen: are there limitations on streaming with function/tool-calls? we use tool calls to enrich responses.

[00:09:46] Ravi: streaming with tool-calls is supported; complexity comes from synchronous tool exec and chunk merging. We'll run a test that includes tool-call latency to measure end-to-end.

[00:10:00] Anna: ok let's recap and align on next steps — Devon, Ravi, can you summarize the bench plan?

[00:10:06] Devon: sure: 1) run a 48-hour token/sec sustained burst test on Hosted regional endpoint in us-central1, with streaming chunks every 16 tokens; 2) run same on a Dedicated reserved pool emulation sized to your expected peak; 3) run a cache-hit focused 24-hour test with 60% template reuse to measure p95 improvements. We'll deliver raw logs, histograms, and a short recommendations doc.

[00:10:36] Ravi: and we'll include quantization A/B at int8 vs fp16 on the Dedicated run for quality vs latency tradeoffs.

[00:10:44] Miguel: I'll share anonymized traces and the synthetic load generator by EOD today.

[00:10:49] Priya: we'll need the security pack and a checklist for Private deployment too.

[00:10:55] Anna: I'll send the security pack and pricing. Action items noted. Any other questions?

[00:11:03] Karen: one last question — can you do a small pilot on Dedicated with a 2-week trial?

[00:11:07] Anna: yes, we'll propose a pilot — usually a short Dedicated reserved trial or hybrid with committed burst credit. We'll include the pilot proposal in the follow-up.

[00:11:16] Omar: sounds good. Thank you all.

[00:11:19] Anna: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with docs and schedule the deep dive.

[00:11:25] (call ends)

Notes about transcription: minor mis-attributions and filler words present, some terms like KV cache or int8 occasionally transcribed as k-v cash or in t8.
